cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a hand-spun cotton open-mesh cloth with tie-dyed indigo resist patterning, consistent with Tiv textile traditions (notably the Tiv are known for exactly this type of indigo tie-dyed cotton cloth, sometimes called "tugudu" style weaves).

physical.title: cloth; waist-cloth
physical.summary: Cloth (an open-mesh sash or waist-cloth), composed of 12 strips of hand-spun cotton sewn together along the selvedges. The strips are identical, each being woven from natural cotton, with the warp threads bunched towards the edges and more loosely separated down the middle; the weft is also widely spaced so that the warp and weft together create an open mesh. The cloth after being assembled was tied and dyed in indigo; this has produced a bold pattern of a central circle of undyed cloth with extensions at the four corners, set against an indigo background. The warp ends have been twisted and knotted to form a fringe.
